blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The House of Representatives on Tuesday passed on second reading a bill prohibiting children aged 13 and below from creating social media accounts while restricting access for those under 18. The measure aligns the Philippines alongside a global shift enacting digital guardrails to shield minors from online harms. Lawmakers approved House Bill No. 11566 by voice vote. The bill, known as the Safe and Friendly Environment for Kids in Digital Spaces Act, consolidates over 40 legislative proposals seeking to enforce tighter oversight over minor social media usage.
